title: fix(google): stop citation requests when a search is cancelled
body:
Supersedes #155494, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cancelling a Gemini web search still allows citation redirect requests to run, including later batches.

## User Impact

Cancelling a Google search cancels active citation requests, prevents further citation requests, and preserves the caller's cancellation reason without caching a late result. Ordinary redirect failures still keep the original citation URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the search's existing AbortSignal to the citation resolver, which owns cancellation checks and guarded HEAD requests. The optional parameter preserves existing one-argument callers. This replacement covers cancellation; the original proposal's citation-admission optimization remains a separate follow-up.

Removed redundant header branching and the single-use header-cache-key binding in the same Google owner, preserving case-insensitive Headers.set precedence. Citation enrichment updates the provider's newly created objects directly, removing duplicate arrays and copies. Production delta: zero lines; tests: +63 lines.

## Evidence

- On main `66e2433288b23cb4c4fef5889f2fbcfcc19f9601`, both cancellation regressions fail: cancellation after the response still starts a HEAD request, and cancellation during the first batch starts all 25 redirects instead of stopping at ten.
- With the fix, all 59 Google provider tests and both existing redirect tests pass on Blacksmith Testbox. The Google file took 55.46 seconds including 46.28 seconds preparing compiled workers; the redirect file took 3.82 seconds. Both named files completed in 64.64 seconds. Tests exercise the provider factory and real citation/guard owners with a controlled fetch boundary; no live Google inference was run.
- Independent autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete local candidate against the same main commit: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. The hosted review of the earlier head raised a scope-only P3 about header cleanup; the final cleanup preserves Headers.set semantics and is retained as same-owner duplicate removal within the net-zero production budget.
- The custom-endpoint regression verifies that provider attribution replaces case-colliding operator headers. It was red on the initial cleanup and green after correction.
- Touched-file lint for the Google runtime/test and citation resolver passes with zero warnings/errors; formatting passes for all four changed source/test/docs files. `git diff --check` passes.
- Added a 63-line test allocation for the production-path cancellation regressions and the custom-endpoint header precedence case. No test ceiling scalar was changed.
- Contributor code was read with `gh` and was never checked out or executed. The fix was reimplemented on main. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41638772489) and the required CI gate passed for `aab7ba6944af3e9bf50b23c11bd4eadcf3efc4af`.
